extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.
NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sets material requirements for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production.

API 6A product specification level (PSL 1 to 4) sets the inspection, testing and traceability applied; PR1 and PR2 are the performance requirement levels, PR2 having passed API 6A design-validation testing. PSL 3G adds a gas test.

faqs.q: What is a 1,440 psi 3-phase well-test separator used for?
faqs.a: A 3-phase well-test separator splits well flow into gas, oil and water so each stream can be measured during a well test. This unit is a 1,440 psi MAWP vessel, 60-inch OD by 15-ft seam-to-seam, ASME U-stamped and built with NACE MR-0175 compliant materials.

faqs.q: What do 60-in OD × 15-ft and 1,440 psi mean on this well-test separator?
faqs.a: 60-in OD × 15-ft is the vessel size: 60 inches outside diameter and 15 feet seam-to-seam, and 1,440 psi is the maximum allowable working pressure (MAWP). The size sets the liquid retention time and gas capacity, so give the flow rates you expect when sizing a variant.

faqs.q: What pressure variants of the 3-phase well-test separator are available?
faqs.a: The 3-phase separator is built in pressure variants of 250, 900, 1,440 and 2,160 psi. This listing is the 1,440 psi, 60-inch OD by 15-ft unit; for a different size or rating, tell us the flow rates and pressure on the RFQ and we engineer the variant.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of the 1,440 psi 3-phase separator, and what is MAWP?
faqs.a: The 3-phase separator is rated 1,440 psi MAWP, the maximum allowable working pressure of the ASME U-stamped vessel. The pressure safety valve (PSV) is fitted to protect it, and operating pressure should stay below the MAWP with the margin your procedure requires.

faqs.q: What materials is the 1,440 psi well-test separator made from, and is it sour-service rated?
faqs.a: The separator is built with NACE MR-0175 compliant materials for sour service, in an ASME U-stamped pressure vessel. Confirm the H2S level and the wetted-material requirements on the RFQ so the internals and trim are matched to the fluid.

faqs.q: Which codes and certificates apply to the 1,440 psi 3-phase separator?
faqs.a: The vessel is ASME U-stamped and the materials are NACE MR-0175 compliant, and the offshore skid is DNV-certified. These are the codes the listing states; third-party witness and the data book scope are agreed on the quotation.

faqs.q: What instruments and valves are fitted to the 3-phase well-test separator?
faqs.a: The separator has a Daniel orifice valve, a pressure safety valve (PSV) and a full suite of process control valves for level, flow and pressure. It connects to the well-test spread through the test line; see the [well testing equipment guide](/blog/surface-well-testing-equipment) for the spread.

faqs.q: How is the 3-phase separator installed on an offshore or onshore well-test spread?
faqs.a: It is mounted on a DNV-certified offshore skid, with an onshore skid variant and trailer-mounted variants integrated into full well-test trailers. Install it downstream of the choke manifold and ahead of the flare and surge tank, per the test layout.

faqs.q: Where is a 60-inch 3-phase well-test separator used?
faqs.a: It is used for multiphase well testing on exploration, appraisal and production wells, where gas, oil and water rates are measured separately. See the [well testing equipment guide](/blog/surface-well-testing-equipment) for the full spread from flowhead to flare.

faqs.q: 3-phase separator or MPFM for well testing: how do they differ?
faqs.a: A 3-phase separator physically splits the gas, oil and water for measurement, while a multiphase flow meter (MPFM) measures the mixed stream without separating it. See the [MPFM system](/c/wt-mpfm-system) shelf for the meter-based option.
